title: Typing Behavior in Human-LLM Interaction: Keystroke Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Effort During Prompting
abstract: arXiv:2606.28090v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into daily routines, understanding how users interact with these systems is crucial for effective human-AI collaboration. This work investigates keystroke dynamics as a behavioral measure of user mental effort and perceived output usefulness in human-LLM interaction. We conducted a user study (N = 36) to examine how task difficulty (easy vs. hard) and device type (desktop vs. mobile) influence typing behavior and workload (NASA-TLX) during interactions. Our results indicate that hard tasks led to significantly more keystrokes, slower typing, increased pauses, and higher self-reported workload. Device type had weaker effects, with mobile use slightly reducing input length and typing speed. translated_title: 人类与大语言模型交互中的打字行为：击键动态揭示提示编写过程中的认知投入
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）日益融入日常生活，理解用户如何与这些系统交互对于实现有效的人机协作至关重要。本研究将击键动态作为衡量用户心理努力程度和感知输出有用性的行为指标。我们开展了一项用户研究（N = 36），考察任务难度（简单与困难）和设备类型（桌面端与移动端）如何影响交互过程中的打字行为与工作负荷（NASA-TLX）。结果表明，困难任务导致击键次数显著增加、打字速度变慢、停顿增多以及更高的自我报告工作负荷。设备类型的影响较弱，移动设备的使用会略微降低输入长度和打字速度。虽然击键能够捕捉认知投入的差异，但无法预测用户对LLM输出有用性的感知。这些发现凸显了击键动态作为实时指标的潜力。
tldr: 该研究通过36人的用户实验发现，击键动态（击键次数、打字速度和停顿时长）可作为反映用户在提示编写过程中认知投入的实时行为指标，对任务难度尤为敏感，但无法预测用户对LLM输出有用性的感知。
en_tdlr: Through a user study (N=36), this work demonstrates that keystroke dynamics—more keystrokes, slower typing, and longer pauses—serve as real-time behavioral indicators of cognitive effort during prompting, sensitive to task difficulty but not predictive of perceived LLM output usefulness.
